2026-12-24.alt: The readings for this day are not in the 2024–25 First Set calendar. Please consult the official 2026–27 Syro-Malabar calendar. The Christmas night celebration follows this evening.
2026-12-24.verse: But you, O Bethlehem of Ephrathah, who are one of the little clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to rule in Israel, whose origin is from of old, from ancient days.
theo: On Christmas Eve the Church looks to Bethlehem, “one of the little clans of Judah”. God chooses the small: a little town, a poor couple, a manger. Bethlehem means “house of bread”; there the Bread of Life is born.

Tonight families gather, lamps and stars are lit, and the parish celebrates the night Qurbana. Let the noise of preparations give way, at least for a few moments, to silent adoration. The One whose origin is from ancient days comes as a baby who can be held.
outline: Ask: why did God choose little Bethlehem?
The Bread of Life is born in Bethlehem.
“From you shall come forth one who is to rule.”
live: Spend five minutes in silence before the crib tonight.
Call or visit someone who will be alone this Christmas.
2026-12-24.prayer: Lord Jesus, born in Bethlehem, the house of bread, come into our homes tonight. Let us adore you in silence and share your love with the lonely. Amen.
altar: Bethlehem, the house of bread, is fulfilled at our altar. The One laid in a manger is given to us in the Holy Qurbana of Christmas night.

quick: God chooses the small: little Bethlehem.
Make room for silent adoration tonight.

2026-12-24.question: Will there be silence for Jesus in my Christmas Eve?

family.explain: God chose little Bethlehem for Jesus to be born. Bethlehem means ‘house of bread’. Jesus came to feed us with his love.
family.intention: We pray for all families gathering tonight, and for those who are alone.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift will each of us give to baby Jesus tonight?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, tonight you come to Bethlehem, the house of bread. As we wait in joy, quiet our hearts and prepare us to adore you. Amen.
share: God chose little Bethlehem (Micah 5:2). Where do I see God choosing the small in my life?
What noise must I silence tonight to adore the Child?
What gift will I bring to the manger?
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that she may welcome Christ with joy tonight.
For families gathering for Christmas, that they may be united in love.
For those who are alone, sick or grieving tonight.
For the poor and homeless, who share the poverty of the stable.
For peace in the Holy Land and in all places of war.
pm.close: Lord God, you chose little Bethlehem for the birth of your Son. Make our hearts a humble stable where he may be born tonight, and fill our homes with his peace. Amen.

illus: In a small parish in the high ranges, the electricity failed just before the midnight Qurbana. The priest continued by candlelight. An old man said afterwards: “For the first time I felt I was in the stable at Bethlehem. Dark, poor, and full of God.”

homily: Dear friends, tonight the whole Church looks to Bethlehem. The prophet Micah had said: but you, O Bethlehem of Ephrathah, who are one of the little clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to rule in Israel, whose origin is from of old, from ancient days (Micah 5:2).

God chooses the small: a little town, a poor couple, a stable, a manger. He does not come in Rome or Jerusalem, but in the margins. This is good news for all who feel small: the village, the poor family, the forgotten person.

Bethlehem means ‘house of bread’. The One who would say ‘I am the bread of life’ is born in the house of bread and laid in a manger, a feeding trough. From the first night, he comes to be food for us.

Tonight our families gather. Stars are hung and lamps are lit. Many will come to the night Qurbana. Let the noise of preparations give way, at least for some moments, to silent adoration before the crib.
The One whose origin is from ancient days comes as a baby who can be held. God makes himself small so that we will not be afraid to come near. Let us come near tonight, with our joys and our wounds.

If you have not yet made your confession, there is still time. If there is someone you have not forgiven, forgive tonight. And when you kneel before the crib, say simply: Lord, you came for me. Welcome. Amen.
kids: Children, tonight baby Jesus is born! Kneel at the crib and tell Him: Jesus, I love you.

intro: Christmas Eve: God chooses the small. (The day's official readings are pending.)

sub: Micah foretold the ruler from Bethlehem.
q: But you, O Bethlehem of Ephrathah, who are one of the little clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to rule in Israel, whose origin is from of old, from ancient days.
And she gave birth to her firstborn son and wrapped him in bands of cloth, and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the inn.
points.apply: Spend five minutes in silence before the crib.

points.h: He shall be the one of peace
sub: The ruler from Bethlehem is a shepherd.
q: And he shall stand and feed his flock in the strength of the LORD… and he shall be the one of peace.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
points.apply: Call someone who will be alone this Christmas.

sub: The Bread of Life is born for us.
q: O taste and see that the LORD is good; happy are those who take refuge in him.
Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry.”
points.apply: Receive Communion at the Christmas Qurbana with deep faith.

concl: God comes in the small and the poor.
Let us adore him in silence.
